help.simple:
Just press one of the buttons, or write normally, e.g. "Please send me a photo".

"View photo" shows you a current picture. Under each photo you can zoom in, make it sharper or brighter.
"View video" shows you the last few seconds.
"Camera status" tells you whether everything is working.

You can always go back with "Back to menu".

web.wg_intro: Phones and laptops with access can reach home from anywhere: the dashboard, the cameras and the ad blocker, as if they were in your Wi-Fi.
web.wg_app_hint: Phones with the PiGuard app need nothing here: the app creates its own access. Tap the shield at the top of the app.
web.pq_intro: Phones and computers fetch a fresh key through the tunnel using ML-KEM-1024 and HQC-256 (hybrid post-quantum key establishment). That key becomes a rotating WireGuard preshared key. It is not the same as a static PSK alone, and WireGuard's handshake remains Curve25519.

web.reach_intro: Any of these can carry you home. Set up one or more: the app tries them in turn. Which one works depends on your internet connection, not on the router brand.
web.reach_check_hint: Checking asks api.ipify.org once for your public address. From inside, pi-guard cannot see whether the router really lets anything through. A test on mobile data shows that.
web.reach_public: Public IPv4 address of this connection: {address}
web.reach_seen: Confirmed: {used} device(s) connected this way from outside right now.
web.reach_v4_off: Not set up. Needs a public IPv4 address, which many cable and fibre connections no longer have (DS-Lite, CGNAT).
web.reach_v4_no_address: This name has no IPv4 address. It may be mistyped, or the connection has no IPv4 of its own. Try IPv6, a rented server or Tailscale.
web.reach_v4_shared: The address {address} is shared by your provider (CGNAT), so nothing can reach you on it. Use IPv6, a rented server or Tailscale.
web.reach_v4_other: The name points to {address}, but this connection goes out as {public}. Either the name is out of date, or the provider shares the address (DS-Lite, CGNAT). In that case use another way.
web.reach_v4_ok: The address looks right. The router must forward UDP to this device. Test it on mobile data.
web.reach_v6_possible: Possible: this device has the public address {address}. It needs a name that follows it and a router rule.
web.reach_v6_none: This device has no public IPv6 address.
web.reach_v6_no_address: This name has no IPv6 address.
web.reach_v6_other: The name points to {address}, which is not this device. With IPv6 it must lead to the Pi itself, not the router.
web.reach_v6_ok: The name leads to this device. The router must let UDP through. Test it on a network with IPv6.
web.reach_relay_off: Not set up. Works with any connection, costs a few euros a month. The server cannot read the VPN.
web.reach_relay_down: The tunnel to the server is down. Is the server running and its port open?
web.reach_relay_ok: The tunnel to the server is up.
web.reach_ts_off: Not installed. Works with any connection, without a router change, but needs a Tailscale account.
web.reach_ts_ok: Running. This device is {address} there. On the phone use the Tailscale app instead of the VPN in PiGuard: Android runs one VPN at a time.
web.reach_how_ipv4: Give the Pi a name that follows your public address (DynDNS, for example from the router or DuckDNS). In the router, forward UDP 51820 to the Pi. Every router can do this, usually under port forwarding or port sharing.
web.reach_how_ipv6: Use a name with the Pi's own IPv6 address, not the router's. In the router, allow UDP 51820 to the Pi over IPv6. The phone's network needs IPv6 too.
web.reach_how_relay: Rent a small Debian or Ubuntu server and log in by ssh once. This command sets up both sides. The Pi dials out, so no router has to change.
web.reach_how_tailscale: Run this on the Pi and log in. Then install the Tailscale app on the phone with the same account.

All as counts per range, from the last seven days. From phones whose users agreed in the app: app and Android versions and crash places.

web.as_model_hint: Small models are cheap and usually good enough.
web.as_location_hint: For the weather, which needs no AI and no key.
web.as_limit_hint: After that the assistant pauses until the next day.
web.as_speech_output: Also read answers aloud (OpenAI only, costs extra)
web.as_privacy: Questions go to the chosen provider. The assistant gets no pictures, names or data from your home and cannot switch anything.

web.conn_public_unknown: The public address could not be checked.
web.sound_bad_name: That name is not possible (a-z, 0-9, _) or already taken.
web.sound_replace_hint: A file with the name of an existing sound replaces it.
web.codeword_hint: Optional: asked in addition at every login, also with passkeys and Telegram.
web.codeword_hint_new: A hint for you (optional). It is shown at login after the password. Leave empty for none.
web.codeword_hint_gives_away: The hint must not contain the code word itself.
web.codeword_too_short: The code word needs at least 4 characters.
web.confirm_password: Please enter your password to confirm
web.recovery_save: Keep these codes safe, e.g. printed. Each works once if the phone with your 2FA codes is gone. They are not shown again.
web.recovery_needs_totp: Available once 2FA codes are set up.
web.recovery_hint: Phone gone? Enter a recovery code here.
web.webauthn_hint: Log in with a YubiKey, fingerprint or the device's face unlock. Very safe, because nothing can be intercepted.
web.webauthn_login: Log in with passkey or key
web.webauthn_cancelled: Cancelled or refused by the device.
web.webauthn_failed: The key could not be verified.
web.webauthn_needs_name: Passkeys and hardware keys do not work on an IP address. The guide below shows how to set up a name.
web.tg_login_wait: Check that Telegram shows the same number, then confirm the login.
web.tg_login_unavailable: Telegram cannot be reached right now.
evidence.failed: The evidence video could not be created.
evidence.started: Evidence video running: {name}, {minutes} minutes. The video follows by itself.
evidence.too_big: The file is too large to send. It is in the dashboard under Events › Evidence videos.
web.notif_intro: Choose which messages you get. Changes apply at once.
web.topo_router_text: Your router connects the home network to the internet and forwards the VPN port to the Pi.
web.topo_pi_text: This Raspberry Pi: recording, detection and dashboard.
web.topo_pihole_text: DNS server and ad blocker for the home network.
web.dev_no_ports: None of the usual ports is open.
web.dev_estimate: This is an estimate from what the device shows on the network.
web.bl_intro: Lists of ad, tracking, malware and phishing domains for Pi-hole. After changes tap “Update lists”.
web.bl_file_hint: One domain per line, hosts format or ||domain^. The domains are blocked one by one.
web.bl_bad_address: That is not a valid link.
web.bl_no_domains: There are no domains in the file.
web.ev_started: Recording ({minutes} minutes). The video appears under Events.
web.ev_who_unclear: face too unclear to say who
web.messenger_test_message: pi-guard test message: this messenger works.
web.messenger_off: This messenger is not set up.
web.messenger_not_delivered: The test message could not be delivered. Is an admin linked there, and is the messenger connected?
web.messengers_intro: Sends a test message to every admin in that messenger, or into the channel of a chat app.
web.push_action_expired: This button is no longer valid. Open pi-guard to do it there.
web.ev_bad_request: Please choose a camera and 1–30 minutes.
web.ev_running: This camera is already recording one.
web.sec_tip_2fa: Recommended: set up 2FA or a passkey (Access).
web.sec_tip_public_2fa: The dashboard is public but has no 2FA or passkey. Please set one up.
web.as_documents_hint: The assistant can search your files, Paperless-ngx and Nextcloud, for admins only. Matching excerpts go to the AI model. With Ollama everything stays in the home network.
web.as_share: Excerpts from documents may go to the cloud provider
web.kn_hint: Upload TXT, MD, JSON or PDF files. They are checked and turned into text, and only matching parts are used per question.
web.kn_not_shared: Files are used only with Ollama, or if you allow sharing with the cloud provider.
knowledge.unsupported: Only TXT, MD, JSON and PDF are supported.
knowledge.too_large: The file is larger than 10 MB.
knowledge.invalid: The file is damaged or not what its ending says.
knowledge.empty: There is no readable text in the file (scanned PDF?).
cmd.expired: This has expired. Nothing was done.
cmd.not_possible: That is not possible right now. Is the feature set up?
cmd.video: Record {minutes} minutes of video from “{camera}” and send it
cmd.record: Record sound from {start} to {end} and send it
cmd.look: Send the picture of “{camera}” to the AI provider and have it described
cmd.state_unknown: There is no value from {name} yet.
cmd.vpn_done: VPN access for {name} is created. The QR code is under Network management › VPN.
cmd.record_too_long: That is too long. {limit} minutes at most.
assistant.no_vision: Looking at camera pictures is not allowed. Turn it on under Add-ons › AI assistant.
web.ai_hello: Tell me what to do, or ask a question. I ask before every action.
web.as_actions: The AI may plan actions (names of devices and cameras go to the provider; simple commands work without this)
web.as_vision: The AI may look at camera pictures (after confirmation the picture is sent to the provider)
web.api_intro: For your own scripts and home automation. A token gives access to the addresses below.
web.api_shown_once: Copy the token now. It is not shown again.
web.api_bad_token: Please give a name and rights.
web.up_hint: Downloads the new signed version from GitHub, checks the signature, installs it, and goes back to the old one if it does not start. The dashboard is part of the software and updated with it.
web.pm_warning: Add-ons are program code and can do everything pi-guard can: cameras, data, microphone. Only install what you understand or whom you trust.
web.pm_upload_hint: The ZIP needs a plugin.json with id, name, version and entry. Guide: docs/plugins.md
web.pm_bad_zip: The ZIP is damaged or has forbidden paths.
web.pp_empty: Add the first person with the button above.
web.pp_profile_note: All optional. Stays on this Pi and is deleted with the person. Recognition does not use it.
web.pp_bad_picture: This picture could not be read.
web.cal_intro: While you are busy in a calendar, pi-guard counts you as away. Whole-day and free entries do not count.
web.cal_phone_on: Phone calendar: {count} busy times from the PiGuard app.
web.cal_phone_off: Phone calendar: in the PiGuard app under App settings, Calendar.
web.cal_how_google_text: On a computer open calendar.google.com, Settings, your calendar on the left, Integrate calendar, and copy the secret address in iCal format.
web.cal_how_proton_text: In Proton Calendar open Settings, Calendars, your calendar, Share, and create a link for anyone. Copy that link.
web.cal_how_other_text: Nextcloud, Outlook, iCloud and many more offer a link to subscribe, usually ending in .ics or starting with webcal://.
web.cal_privacy: Such a link works like a password. It is kept on this Pi and not shown again. Only start and end of busy times are stored, no titles, places or people.
web.cal_bad_link: This does not look like a calendar link. It must start with https:// or webcal://.
web.cal_not_a_calendar: There is no calendar behind this link.
web.cal_bad_name: Please enter a name. At most ten calendars are possible.
web.pp_intro: {count} face prints, added by {by}. Photos are not stored, only numbers from which no picture can be rebuilt.
web.pp_sample: {numbers} numbers, {bytes} bytes, {match} % match with the others
web.nm_no_router: Enter the FRITZ!Box password under Settings › Integrations to see all Wi-Fi networks including guest Wi-Fi.
web.nm_blocks_hint: Blocks a site with all its subdomains, for everyone or one device, for good or for a while.
web.nm_bad_domain: That is not a valid website.
web.nm_needs_addon: Turn on network management for this:
web.nm_page_on: Block page active on {ip}. For HTTPS the pi-guard certificate must be installed on the device.
web.nm_page_off: Without a block page the browser just says “cannot be reached”. Set up: sudo ./scripts/blockpage.sh setup <free-IP>
web.ex_data_hint: Events, log, users, cameras, people (names only), VPN devices, blocks and device names. Keys, tokens and face data are left out. CSV comes as a ZIP with one file per section.
web.ex_config_hint: config.json holds all settings and can be read in again here or on a new device.
web.ex_secrets: Include passwords and tokens (treat the file like a key then)
web.ex_bad_file: This is not a valid config.json.
web.addon_agents_text: Servers and computers at a glance: status, security check, updates, Docker, Compose and Git with the agent, safe shutdown with two confirmations, and services watched for outages. No open port needed.
web.addon_languages_text: Translates Pi-Guard into more languages with DeepL.
web.ag_intro: The agent connects to Pi-Guard by itself. It only knows fixed commands and gives nobody a shell.
web.bk_no_passphrase: Set a backup passphrase first. Backups are encrypted with it, and without it nobody can restore them: keep it apart, for example in a password manager.
web.bk_ssh_hint: For rsync and Borg: add this line to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys of the user on the server.
web.bk_restore_hint: To restore: pi-guard backup restore FILE asks for the passphrase and unpacks into a folder; see docs/backup.md.
web.addon_medical_text: Medical information of the people at home: allergies, illnesses, medicines and plans, encrypted, seen only with the password, and shared with rescuers by a short-lived link.
web.md_intro: Only admins see these, and only with their password each time. Every look, change and link is in the audit log.
web.md_form_intro: Everything except the name is optional. What can harm the person if nobody knows it comes first on the rescue page.
web.md_privacy: Health data are encrypted on this pi-guard and never go into push messages or MQTT. They reach a chat only when you send them to an emergency contact, or an SOS does for a contact set to get them: as a rescue link with a PIN, or as a PDF if you chose that. They are part of the data export.
web.md_pin_ask: Enter the PIN you were told.
web.md_pin_wrong: Wrong PIN. After five wrong ones the link ends.
web.md_sheet_intro: Emergency information given by the household, read only.
web.sv_started: Started. The computer works on it in the background.
web.sv_warn_ssh_root_password: SSH lets root log in with a password.
web.sv_warn_ssh_passwords: SSH accepts passwords. Keys only are safer.
web.sv_warn_failed_logins: Many failed logins in the last 24 hours.
web.sv_secure: Nothing found that needs a look.
web.sv_no_manager: No known package manager (apt, pacman, dnf).
web.sv_needs: Switched off on that computer. To allow it, add {key} to /etc/pi-guard-agent/agent.conf there.
web.ag_token_once: Run this on the home server. The token is not shown again. The script shows a fingerprint; compare it with the file /ca.crt.
web.ag_offline: This home server is not connected right now.
web.ag_timeout: The home server did not answer.
web.lg_intro: Choose languages. All texts are translated once with DeepL and stored on the Pi. The language can then be chosen under Settings › General.
web.lg_no_key: You need a DeepL key for this.
web.lg_hint: Machine translation can be clumsy. New texts appear in English until you install the language again.
web.pm_git_failed: The repository could not be loaded.
web.tip_signal_commands: Off: Signal only sends alerts and reads no message, also not from you. Right for a private number
web.account_viewer_hint: Here you change your own password and second factor.
web.viewer_forbidden: Your account can only watch. Ask an admin.
web.user_taken: This user name is already taken.
web.users_hint: Admins may do everything, viewers only watch, members watch and use what you grant them.
web.users_delete: Remove {name}? This person is signed out at once.
web.ap_everyone_hint: These apply to all users and devices, also on the login page.
web.ap_name_hint: Shown in the browser tab, the installed app and the desktop app, for example to keep it inconspicuous. On the phone, choose name and icon in the app under App settings.
web.webauthn_err_denied: Cancelled, timed out, or refused by the browser.
web.webauthn_err_host: The browser does not accept this address for keys. Open the dashboard by its name.
web.webauthn_err_support: This browser or key does not support this.
web.webauthn_err_cert: The browser does not trust the certificate. Install the pi-guard certificate (step 2 below) and restart the browser.
web.key_guide_name: Open the dashboard by a name, not an IP address. On the Pi this creates the name in Pi-hole:
web.key_guide_ca: Make this computer trust the certificate:
web.key_guide_touch: Restart the browser, open the name, press Add and touch the key when it blinks.
scan.started: The security scan is running. You will get the report here, it can take a few minutes.
scan.running: A security scan is already running.
storage.title: {free} GB of {total} GB free. Largest items:

web.tip_nav_overview: Everything at a glance: state, cameras and recent events
web.tip_nav_live: The live picture of a camera, with listening and talking
web.tip_nav_events: What happened, with pictures and statistics
web.tip_nav_network: Devices, Wi-Fi, VPN, Pi-hole and the map
web.tip_nav_logs: What the system did, and who logged in
web.tip_mode_home: Someone is at home: fewer alerts
web.tip_mode_away: Nobody is at home: motion and people raise alerts
web.tip_mode_auto: Follows who is at home by their phones
web.tip_sharper: Combines several pictures into a sharper one
web.tip_listen: Hear the microphone of this camera
web.tip_recording_max_storage_percent: Above this level the oldest recordings are deleted, those without motion first
web.tip_recording_continuous: Records all the time, not only on motion
web.tip_motion_sensitivity: Higher reacts to smaller movements, but also to more false alarms
web.tip_person_detection_enabled: Tells people apart from pets and shadows
web.tip_face_recognition_enabled: Recognises trusted people. Stored only on this system
web.tip_presence_enabled: Switches between home and away by phones in the Wi-Fi
web.tip_signal_phone_number: The Signal number pi-guard writes from. With your own number, use Note to Self
web.tip_signal_admin_numbers: These numbers may use every command
web.tip_signal_allowed_numbers: These numbers may watch and receive alerts
web.tip_signal_cli_address: Address of the local signal-cli service. Usually stays as it is
web.tip_telegram_admin_user_ids: Telegram users who may use every command
web.tip_telegram_viewer_user_ids: Telegram users who may watch and receive alerts
web.tip_emergency_telegram_user_ids: Get a message when alerts stay unanswered
web.tip_emergency_signal_numbers: Get a message when alerts stay unanswered
web.ap_nav_hint: Drag entries to your order. It is saved for your account. On phones the first four appear at the bottom.
web.signal_missing: signal-cli is not installed. Run this on the Pi:
web.signal_stopped: signal-cli is installed but does not start. Run the installation again on the Pi:
web.signal_unlinked: signal-cli is running. Now link your phone.
web.signal_restart: Your phone is linked and your number is saved. Restart pi-guard to finish.
web.signal_success: Done! Your phone is linked with Signal.
web.signal_success_next: Signal is still taking over your data, which can take a minute. Restart pi-guard once to finish. Messages from pi-guard then arrive in Note to Self.
web.signal_busy: Signal is busy taking over data from your phone. This can take a minute and fixes itself.
web.signal_after_scan: After scanning, linking takes up to half a minute. This page shows when it is done.
web.signal_test_sent: Sent. Look in Note to Self in Signal.
web.signal_test_failed: The test message could not be sent. Try again in a minute.
web.mob_map_failed: The map could not be loaded.
web.signal_link_tip: Shows a QR code for Signal on your phone
web.signal_scan: In Signal on your phone: Settings, Linked devices, Link new device. Then scan this code.
web.wifi_no_fritz: No FRITZ!Box connected. Enter the name and key by hand.
web.wifi_no_key: The FRITZ!Box did not answer. Check the password and rights of its user.
web.wifi_bad_input: The name is missing, or the key does not have 8 to 63 characters.
web.wifi_pi_on_wifi: This Pi uses the Wi-Fi itself, a new key would cut it off. Change it on the FRITZ!Box.
web.wifi_scan: Scan this code with the camera of a phone to join.
web.wifi_save_tip: Saves the code as a picture. Anyone with it can join this Wi-Fi
web.wifi_qr_tip: QR code to join this Wi-Fi
web.wifi_renew_tip: Everyone on this Wi-Fi has to join again
web.wifi_renew_confirm: All devices are thrown out of your Wi-Fi at once, also yours, and need the new key. Devices you do not give it to can then only use the guest Wi-Fi. Continue?
web.wifi_renew_guest_confirm: All devices in the guest Wi-Fi have to join again with the new key. Continue?
web.ia_allowed: This device may use the internet.
web.ia_blocked: This device is blocked from the internet.
web.ia_tip: Set on the FRITZ!Box for this address
web.ia_confirm: Block the internet for {ip}? The device stays in the Wi-Fi.
web.ia_hint: The FRITZ!Box offers no way to throw out a single device. To make everyone join again, use New key in the Wi-Fi list.
web.ex_title: What others can see of you
web.ex_teaser: See what your internet provider and others in the network can find out about this device.
web.ex_tip: Uses what this Pi knows about the device you are using now
web.ex_vpn: You are connected through the VPN. Where you are now, the local network only sees encrypted traffic to your home. From your home, everything below still applies.
web.ex_p_ip: Which servers your home connects to, and when
web.ex_p_dns: Every website name you look up: DNS leaves your home unencrypted
web.ex_p_dns_hidden: Website names you look up stay hidden: DNS is encrypted
web.ex_p_sni: Usually the website name again when connecting, even with HTTPS
web.ex_p_content: Not what you read or send on HTTPS pages
web.ex_o_services: Services your device offers, such as shared folders
web.ex_o_content: Not your traffic on an encrypted Wi-Fi with a normal router
web.ex_a_domains: All domains this device asks for, through Pi-hole
web.ex_a_content: Not the content of encrypted connections
web.ex_example: For example, from your last {count} lookups
web.ex_estimate: A general estimate plus what this Pi sees. Nothing is sent anywhere.
web.plan_intro: Mark when nobody is usually at home, for example at work. pi-guard then switches to Away and back.
web.plan_on_tip: Off keeps the plan but does not switch
web.plan_presence: Stay at Home if someone is detected at home
web.plan_presence_tip: A phone in the Wi-Fi stops the switch to Away
web.plan_hint: Drag in a day to mark time, tap a block to change it. If you change the mode by hand, that stays until the next change in the plan.
web.support_hint: Who helps when something does not work. Shown small on the overview, in settings, logs and the assistant. All optional.
web.scan_intro: Checks updates, firewall, open ports, changed files, signs of rootkits and your login. Takes a few minutes and changes nothing.
web.scan_no_job: Only pi-guard itself can be checked: the root job is not installed. Run scripts/install.sh again.
web.scan_report: Send the report to admins by messenger
web.scan_report_tip: Short summary by Telegram, Signal or WhatsApp
web.scan_wait: This can take several minutes. You can leave this page.
web.scan_second_factor_fix: Set up a code app or hardware key under Access.
web.scan_tls_fix: Switch on HTTPS under Settings, Dashboard.
web.scan_integrity_fix: Files changed since installing. Run scripts/install.sh again and find out why.
web.scan_ports_fix: Check whether you need these ports and close them otherwise.
web.scan_root_job_fix: The root job did not answer. Run scripts/install.sh again.
web.scan_reboot_fix: An update needs a restart of the Pi.
web.scan_firewall_fix: Switch on a firewall such as ufw. First allow SSH, or you lock yourself out.
web.scan_ssh_fix: Use SSH keys and set PasswordAuthentication no and PermitRootLogin no.
web.scan_system_files_fix: These files differ from their package. That can be harmless; check them.
web.scan_suid: No unknown programs with root rights
web.scan_suid_fix: These programs run with root rights and belong to no package. Check them at once.
web.scan_suspicious: No suspicious programs in temporary folders
web.scan_suspicious_fix: Find out where these files come from.
web.scan_accounts_fix: There are extra root accounts or accounts without a password.
web.scan_rootkits_fix: No scanner installed. For a deeper check: sudo apt install rkhunter
web.st_intro: Recordings older than {days} days are removed automatically. If the disk runs short before that, the oldest recordings without motion go first, so there is always room for new ones.
web.st_days: Delete {name} older than how many days?
web.st_confirm: Really delete {name} older than {days} days? This cannot be undone.
web.st_vacuum_confirm: Compact the database? No data is removed.
web.st_evidence_note: Evidence videos and face data are not cleaned here on purpose.
web.st_apt_tip: Downloaded packages, they can be fetched again
web.st_journal_confirm: Delete system logs older than 14 days?
web.st_no_job: The root job is not installed.
web.st_busy: The database is busy. Try again in a moment.
web.tip_discord_bot_token: Developer Portal, under Bot, Reset Token. Not the Client Secret or Public Key
web.tip_discord_admin_user_ids: These people may use every command and get alerts
web.tip_discord_viewer_user_ids: These people may watch and get alerts
web.tip_emergency_discord_user_ids: Get a message when alerts stay unanswered
web.addon_discord_text: Commands, photos and alerts through a Discord bot, like with Telegram.
web.discord_setup: Enter the token and your user ID above, switch on Discord and save. The guide is in docs/discord.md.
web.discord_waiting: Not connected yet. After saving, restart pi-guard. If it stays like this, check the token.
web.discord_invite_tip: Needed once: Discord only lets bots write to people who share a server with them
web.discord_test_tip: Sends a message to all Discord admins
web.discord_not_delivered: Could not be delivered. Is the bot on a server with this person, and are direct messages allowed?
web.dev_test_speaker_tip: Plays three short tones on the chosen speaker
web.dev_test_mic_tip: Records 3 seconds for you to hear. Nothing is kept
web.dev_test_heard: Did you hear three tones? Then this is the right speaker.
web.dev_test_silent: Almost nothing was heard. Try another microphone, or speak closer to it.
web.dev_test_sound: Sound was picked up, loudest moment {peak} dB. Listen to it here.
web.dev_test_busy: This device is in use right now, for example by a camera.
web.dev_test_failed: The test did not work with this device.
discord.test: Test message from pi-guard: Discord works.
web.tip_dashboard_auth_password: User name and password, with a second factor if set up
web.tip_dashboard_auth_keyfile: Log in by choosing a key file
web.tip_dashboard_auth_telegram: The bot asks you in Telegram to confirm the login
web.tip_dashboard_auth_webauthn: A YubiKey, fingerprint or face of the device
faces.tip_front: {count} more pictures looking at the camera
faces.tip_left: {count} pictures with the head turned a little to the left
faces.tip_right: {count} pictures with the head turned a little to the right
faces.tip_light: Pictures in different light, for example in the evening
faces.tip_mixed: The pictures differ a lot. Look at the details and delete odd ones
faces.tip_similar: Looks a lot like {other}: add pictures from the cameras at home
web.pq_tip: An estimate from the number and variety of pictures. The test with a photo shows the real result
web.tip_fritzbox_username: The user set up on the FRITZ!Box. Empty: the box names its last user
web.discord_refused: Discord refused the token. Under Bot in the Developer Portal, press Reset Token and paste the new one. The Client Secret and Public Key are other values.
web.discord_bad_token: This is not a bot token, probably the Client Secret. In the Developer Portal, open Bot and press Reset Token.
web.addon_whatsapp_text: Commands and alerts through the official WhatsApp Cloud API.
web.addon_email_text: Alerts and data exports by email. Commands stay with the chat messengers.
web.addon_chatapps_text: Alerts as cards into other services. Send-only and without pictures: what your cameras see stays out of them.
web.ag_docker_remove_confirm: Remove “{name}”? The container stops and is deleted. Its image and named volumes stay.
web.addon_remove_tip: Switches it off and deletes its settings and data
web.addon_remove_confirm: Remove {name}? Its settings and data are deleted.
web.as_usage_note: Counted here for {model}, without speech. Your bill at the provider is what counts.
web.as_usage_prices_hint: Providers do not tell a normal key its balance, so pi-guard counts itself. Take the prices of your model from the provider's price list.
web.as_budget_hint: What you put on the account. pi-guard subtracts what it counted since then.
web.tip_email_export: The file holds events, logs and names. Email is not end-to-end encrypted
web.email_hint: After saving and restarting you can try it out here.
web.email_test_tip: Sends a message to all recipients
web.email_export_tip: Sends all stored data as a file to all recipients
web.email_off: Email is not active. Save and restart first.
web.email_failed: Sending failed. Check server, port, encryption and login.
email.test: Test message from pi-guard: email works.
web.pm_auto_tip: Looks for a new version once a day. It takes effect after a restart
web.pm_auto_confirm: New code from this repository would then be installed without anyone checking it first, with all the rights of pi-guard. Do you trust {name} that much?
web.donate_text: pi-guard is free. If you want to, you can support its development with a donation. Entirely optional.
help.findphone: /findphone name – ring a phone and show where it is
web.addon_mobile_text: The dashboard as an Android app, with alerts, VPN, finding phones and an emergency button.
web.mobile_home_only: New phones can only be connected from the home network or the VPN.
web.mobile_bad_apk: This is not a valid app file.
web.mobile_offline: This phone is offline right now.
web.mob_find_tip: Rings and vibrates at full volume and sends its location
web.mob_map_tip: Show on the map. The tiles load from OpenStreetMap
web.pf_intro: All optional. The email address is also where a login code by email goes. Stored only on this pi-guard.
web.code_intro: pi-guard sends a code to your own accounts there. Your code word or two-factor code is asked afterwards.
web.code_sent: The code went to {channel}. It is valid for 5 minutes.
web.code_message:
pi-guard login code: {code}
From {ip} ({agent}). If that was not you, ignore this message.
web.code_expired: This code has expired. Ask for a new one.
web.code_no_channel: No code can be sent there.
web.code_not_delivered: The code could not be delivered.

web.priv_install_intro: Optional multi-hop exit, DNS fail-closed and Tor control need a one-time root install. This does not install Tor or commercial VPN packages.
web.priv_profiles_intro: Starting points you can change. They are not guaranteed anonymity levels.
web.priv_profile_standard_intro: Home WireGuard only. No upstream exit, Tor or extra obfuscation.
web.priv_profile_enhanced_intro: VPN-routed DNS and an optional kill switch. Add an exit hop when you want multi-hop.
web.priv_profile_maximum_intro: Strict fail-closed. Add a compatible exit (or Tor) before activating, or clients lose internet through the Pi.
web.priv_conn_intro: Activates the upstream chain on this Pi. Devices still connect to the home VPN as usual.
web.priv_recovery: If the Pi lock-out ever blocks management: sudo ./scripts/privacy-server.sh unlock
web.priv_chain_intro: Traffic leaves home through these exits in order. Device → Pi → hop(s) → internet.
web.priv_chain_empty_ui: No hops yet. Link Mullvad or add a custom WireGuard server, then add a hop.
web.priv_chain_limit: Independent nested tunnels beyond Mullvad native multi-hop or a single custom exit are refused rather than silently faked.
web.priv_providers_intro: Mullvad and your own WireGuard servers. Account numbers and private keys stay sealed on the Pi.
web.priv_dns_intro: How DNS is resolved for privacy routing. Strict mode refuses cleartext fallback.
web.priv_dns_strict_hint: When on, unprotected DNS is not used as a silent fallback.
web.priv_ks_intro: Fail-closed forwarding on the Pi when the upstream exit drops. Separate from the kill switch in the desktop app.
web.priv_ks_recovery: Recovery: sudo ./scripts/privacy-server.sh unlock — management from the LAN stays allowed.
web.priv_tor_intro: Optional. Tor is not installed automatically. SOCKS for apps, or VPN-then-Tor when no WireGuard exit hop is active.
web.priv_tor_warning: Routing through Tor is not the same as Tor Browser. It does not hide browser fingerprints and adds high latency.
web.priv_tor_bridges_prompt: Bridge lines (obfs4 / snowflake / webtunnel), one per line
web.priv_obfs_intro: Only modes this Pi can actually run are enabled. Stock Raspberry Pi kernels have no AmneziaWG.
web.priv_obfs_warning: Obfuscation does not guarantee you are invisible to an ISP or traffic analysis.
web.priv_diag_intro: Live status of privacy layers. Exit IP check asks api.ipify.org once.
web.priv_need_tor: Tor is not installed on this Pi
web.priv_need_amnezia: AmneziaWG is not available on this kernel
web.priv_need_dot: No local DoT resolver (systemd-resolved or unbound)
web.priv_doh_later: DNS over HTTPS needs a local resolver not shipped yet
web.priv_doq_later: DNS over QUIC needs a local resolver not shipped yet
web.priv_config_newer: Privacy config is from a newer pi-guard
web.priv_nothing_to_activate: Add an exit hop or enable Tor first
web.priv_chain_unsupported: This hop combination is not supported
web.priv_tor_with_wg_exit: Tor exit cannot be combined with a WireGuard exit hop
web.priv_tor_with_hops: Clear the multi-hop chain before enabling VPN-then-Tor
web.priv_tor_not_a_hop: Use the Tor section; Tor is not a chain hop
web.priv_loop_home: Exit endpoint must not be the home VPN itself
web.priv_loop_subnet: Exit allowed IPs must not swallow the home VPN subnet
web.priv_mullvad_too_many: At most two Mullvad hops (native multi-hop)
web.priv_mullvad_same: Mullvad entry and exit must differ
web.priv_dns_need_servers: Custom DNS needs at least one server
web.priv_dns_strict_system: Strict DNS cannot use unprotected system DNS
web.priv_dns_no_provider: No provider DNS until an exit is configured
web.priv_server_taken: A server with this name already exists
web.priv_key_lost: Stored key cannot be opened (dashboard secret changed?)
web.priv_ssh_preview: SSH provisioning shows a plan only. Apply is not automated in this release.
web.priv_ssh_manual: Use a custom WireGuard import or configure the remote server yourself

web.tip_nav_help: Every part of pi-guard in a few sentences, and a guided tour
web.tut_intro: pi-guard watches your home with your own cameras, tells you what happens, and keeps the network safe. Here is every part in a few sentences.
web.tut_ask: You can also ask the assistant, by chat or voice: "How does Kid Protect work?" or "Tutorial". In chats, /tutorial sends this overview.
web.tut_more: The dashboard, the desktop app and the phone app show the same pages; this help is in all of them. The full documentation is on GitHub.
web.tut_overview_text: Whether everything is fine at a glance. Switch between at home and away here; away, pi-guard reports movement and people.
web.tut_live_text: The live picture of your cameras, with listening, talking and photos. The camera room shows all cameras at once.
web.tut_events_text: Everything that happened: movement, people and evidence videos. "Who is this?" on a person event teaches pi-guard a face.
web.tut_people_text: Who belongs to the family, with their consent. Swipe through faces of recent events: right for yes, left for no.
web.tut_network_text: The state of the home network: devices, Pi-hole, Wi-Fi with QR codes, blocking websites and block lists.
web.tut_vpn_text: Reach home from anywhere. Add a device, scan its QR code, done; the phone app makes its own access.
web.tut_kids_text: Filters for children's devices (18+, gambling, malware and more) and times without internet, such as at night. Pause and extra time with one tap.
web.tut_emergency_text: Who hears from pi-guard after an SOS from a phone or unanswered alarms, and what each gets: place, pictures, events, emergency data.
web.tut_medical_text: Medical information for rescuers: allergies, medicines like on the federal medication plan, organ donation. As a rescue link with PIN, PDF or picture.
web.tut_apps_text: The phone app brings alerts, SOS, quick actions and the VPN; the desktop app shows the dashboard in its own window.
web.tut_assistant_text: Ask questions by chat or voice, also about pi-guard itself. With an AI provider it also explains and changes settings, always with a confirmation.
web.tut_move_text: New home, router or Pi: download a moving file before, and afterwards pi-guard checks what changed and what to do.
web.tut_settings_text: Everything else: messengers, recording, backup, updates, appearance. The accessibility button at the bottom right is always there.
web.set_general_hint: Language, time zone and map. The helper below answers questions about settings.
web.set_recording_hint: How long and in which quality the cameras record.
web.set_detection_hint: When motion, people and faces are detected.
web.set_modes_hint: Home, away and night: what happens in each mode, also on a schedule.
web.set_messaging_hint: Which messengers pi-guard writes through and who may answer.
web.set_notifications_hint: Which messages come, to whom and at what times.
web.set_emergency_hint: Emergency contacts and what they get when it matters.
web.set_access_hint: Accounts, passkeys, recovery and API access.
web.set_appearance_hint: Colours, text and navigation, for this device only.
web.set_data_hint: Backups, disk space, moving and export in one place.
web.set_security_hint: Checks firewall, updates, open ports and SSH on the Pi.
web.set_integrations_hint: Router, Pi-hole, MQTT and other services on the network.
web.set_dashboard_hint: Address, certificate and login of the dashboard.
web.set_support_hint: Who to call or write to with questions.
web.priv_mullvad_expired: The Mullvad account has no paid time left. Please extend it at Mullvad first.
web.priv_mullvad_multihop_on: Multi-hop: in through the first server, out through the second.
web.priv_mullvad_exit_hint: The VPN devices appear on the internet with this address.
web.priv_mullvad_multihop_hint: Mullvad's own multi-hop: the entry sees who you are, the exit where you go, neither both. A little slower.
web.reach_awg_off: Not set up. For networks that recognise and block WireGuard (hotels, offices, some countries): the same connection, wrapped differently.
web.reach_awg_down: Set up, but awg0 is not running. sudo ./scripts/amneziawg.sh status says more.
web.reach_awg_ok: Running on UDP {port}. Forward UDP {port} on the router to the Pi. App 1.8 and newer take this way when the normal ones do not answer.
web.reach_how_awg: Run this on the Pi. It builds AmneziaWG from a fixed, checked version, sets up awg0 next to wg0 and opens the port in ufw. Then forward the UDP port on the router to the Pi and restart pi-guard.
web.ap_reset_hint: Theme, text size and navigation order on this device, and as admin the colour, font, name and animations for everyone.
web.ap_reset_confirm: Really reset the appearance to the default? This cannot be undone.
web.priv_dns_strict_tip: Off: if the protected DNS route (Mullvad, DoT, through the VPN) fails, the Pi quietly asks your provider's normal DNS server, and the internet keeps working, but your provider sees every address again. On: names are not resolved at all until the protected route is back. Safer, but no internet while it is gone.
web.set_apps_hint: Web dashboard, Android app and desktop app: devices, versions and invitations.
web.group_mobile_hint: The Android app is part of pi-guard and on by default: alerts, VPN, finding the phone and the emergency button.
web.addon_telegram_text: Commands, photos, videos and alerts through a Telegram bot. The usual way to be notified.
web.addon_signal_text: Alerts and commands through Signal, end-to-end encrypted, with signal-cli on the Pi.
web.apps_versions_hint: What this Pi hands to your devices. They fetch new versions themselves and install new major and minor versions on their own.
web.apps_invite_hint: A link to download the Android and desktop app, valid for {days} days. It opens only the downloads: to log in, the person needs an account of their own. It works at home and over the VPN.
web.apps_invite_ready: Link created, valid for {days} days. Copy and share it:
web.apps_invite_text: Get the pi-guard app: {url} (valid for {days} days, at home or over the VPN)
web.pm_develop: Develop and publish your own add-ons:
web.addon_agents_help:
Connects PCs, servers and NAS to pi-guard with a small agent.

**To start:**
1. Switch the add-on on and open it.
2. *Add agent* and run the command shown on the computer.
3. You then see its status, updates, Docker and its security check.

Shutting down and other commands always need a double confirmation.
web.addon_remote_help:
Fixed commands chosen beforehand on connected computers, for example *shut the PC down* so its encrypted disk is protected.

1. Set up the *Server* add-on first.
2. Choose the allowed commands here.
3. They run only after a double confirmation, from the dashboard or the chat.

There are no free-form commands, on purpose.
web.addon_analytics_help:
Network management with Pi-hole: which devices are at home, what they ask for, and blocking websites, also for one device or for a while.

1. Connect Pi-hole (*Settings › Network*).
2. Switch the add-on on.
3. Everything else is under *Network*.
web.addon_proxy_help:
An own reverse proxy to reach services behind NAT through a server of your choice, like frp.

The server decides which ports a client may open; tokens are kept there as hashes only. pi-guard opens no router ports for it.
web.addon_smarthome_help:
Switch lamps and plugs and read sensors over MQTT (Zigbee2MQTT, Tasmota, ESPHome).

1. Enter your MQTT broker (*Settings › Integrations*).
2. Switch the add-on on and add devices.
3. Then it works from the chat and the assistant too, e.g. "hall light off".
web.addon_kids_help:
Protection for children's devices: filters for adult content, gambling and malware through Pi-hole, and times without internet through the FRITZ!Box.

1. Connect Pi-hole and/or the FRITZ!Box.
2. Add a child and its devices.
3. Choose filters and times.
web.addon_medical_help:
Emergency data of the people at home: allergies, conditions, medication and the medication plan, stored encrypted.

Logged in, you see the emergency card without another password. In an SOS the data go to the emergency contacts you allow.
web.addon_assistant_help:
Questions in plain language, in the chat, the dashboard or spoken: "What happened today?", "Who was at the door last?".

1. Choose a provider (local with Ollama or a cloud service) and enter its key.
2. Decide what the assistant may see.
3. Spoken questions only get answers, never actions.
web.addon_languages_help: More languages for the dashboard and the chat, translated with DeepL or the assistant. German and English are always there.
web.addon_heartbeat_help: Watches websites, ports and devices and tells you when something goes down.
web.addon_telegram_help:
The usual way for alerts, photos, videos and commands.

1. Create a bot with @BotFather and copy its token.
2. Enter it under *Settings › Messengers*.
3. Write to the bot: the first person becomes admin.
web.addon_signal_help:
Alerts and commands over Signal, end-to-end encrypted. Needs signal-cli on the Pi and a number of its own.

1. Switch the add-on on.
2. Link the number under *Settings › Messengers*.
web.addon_discord_help:
Alerts, photos and commands through a Discord bot.

1. Create a bot in the Discord developer portal.
2. Enter its token and your user ID under *Settings › Messengers*.
web.addon_whatsapp_help: Alerts through Meta's WhatsApp Cloud API. Needs a Meta business account, a number and an approved template for alerts.
web.addon_email_help: Alerts and reports by email, through your own mail server (SMTP).
web.addon_chatapps_help: Alerts as cards to Slack, Matrix, Rocket.Chat or Mastodon. Send only and without pictures: what your cameras see stays out.

web.as_watch: Look at alarm pictures and assess them
web.as_watch_hint: After an alarm the assistant looks at the alarm picture, together with what the face recognition on the Pi knows about trusted people, and sends you a short assessment, also in the message to your emergency contacts. At most every 10 minutes. The reference pictures of your trusted people stay on the Pi.
web.as_watch_confirm: Every alarm picture then goes to your AI provider without asking (with Ollama it stays at home). Switch it on?
web.scan_rootkits_missing_fix: No scanner installed. For a deeper check: sudo apt install rkhunter
web.scan_rootkits_found_fix: rkhunter reports something. Check the lines above: after an update or an install, changed files are often harmless. Once everything is explained, “Accept the rkhunter state” below takes the current state as the new normal.
web.fix_hint: Fixed, tested corrections for the result above. Each makes a backup first and can be undone. Nothing runs without two confirmations and your password.
web.fix_undo_confirm: Undo {name}? The earlier state comes back.
web.fix_type: To confirm a second time, type the name of the fix: {id}
web.fix_confirm_wrong: The name typed does not match. Nothing was changed.
web.scan_fix_confirm_wrong: The name typed does not match. Nothing was changed.
web.fix_started: Started. The result appears here in a moment.
web.fix_ssh-root_what: Sets PermitRootLogin no. You keep logging in with your own user.
web.fix_ssh-passwords_what: Switches passwords off for SSH. Only possible when an SSH key is set up, or you would lock yourself out.
web.fix_rkhunter_what: Takes the current state of the system files as normal (rkhunter --propupd). Only when every warning is explained.
web.fix_firewall_what: Switches ufw on. Everything reachable on the network today and SSH stay open; new things are blocked.
web.review_hint: The assistant looks at the latest result and suggests steps. It gets only statuses and short details, no files and no keys.
web.review_confirm: The latest result (statuses and short details) goes to your AI provider. Continue?
web.review_commands: Commands to run yourself (never run automatically):
web.review_note: An AI's suggestions can be wrong. Only the fixed fixes above run from here; check and start any other command yourself.
web.scan_none_yet: No result yet: run the check first.
web.log_search_audit: Search by person, action or detail …
web.audit_hint: Who did what and when: logins, settings, access. Never changed.
web.tip_update_repository: Where updates come from, e.g. for your own fork. Only what the keys stored on the Pi signed is installed either way
web.tip_update_channel: Stable: finished versions only. Beta: also pre-releases for testing, earlier but riskier
web.up_instance_hint: A random name of this installation, made at the first start. It never leaves the Pi.
web.up_apps_none: No apps on this Pi yet.
web.push_in_android: This app gets alerts over its own connection to the Pi, without Google. Adjust them in the app settings.
web.push_in_desktop: The desktop app has no push notifications. You get alerts through the phone app or a messenger (Add-ons).
